study_identification_part.si4_title: Lifespan development of thalamic nuclei and characterizing thalamic nuclei abnormalities in schizophrenia using normative modeling

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: Model lifespan developmental trajectories of thalamic nuclei volumes using normative modeling and quantify individual-level deviations in an independent schizophrenia cohort; assess associations with cognition.

rci1_dataset_name.reason: The normative reference uses HCP Lifespan datasets spanning Development, Young Adult (S1200), and Aging.
rci1_dataset_name.supporting_text: Normative models generated from the Human Connectome Project Lifespan datasets (5–100+ years)

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis: Group comparisons of centile distributions (Wilcoxon rank-sum for median centiles; chi-square tests with FDR correction for proportions of infra/supra/normal). Spearman correlations between centiles (and standardized raw volumes) and cognitive measures in SZ; GEE models for associations between executive function and nuclei volumes across HCP age groups (with covariates sex, eTIV, family).
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: Up to ~18% of individuals with schizophrenia showed infra-normal (below 5th centile) mediodorsal and pulvinar volumes; deviations (centiles), but not raw volumes, correlated with cognitive impairment severity.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: Normative GAMLSS models revealed heterogeneous lifespan trajectories across nuclei. Applying centile thresholds to the SZ cohort showed elevated infra-normal frequencies primarily in mediodorsal and pulvinar (e.g., up to 18% SZ infra-normal). Wilcoxon tests indicated lower median centiles in SZ for specific nuclei; chi-square tests (with FDR) showed significant group differences in infra/supra/normal proportions for selected nuclei. In SZ, Spearman correlations showed deviation scores had stronger associations with cognition than standardized raw volumes.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: Neuroimaging pipelines containerized with Singularity; thalamic segmentation via THOMAS; code for analyses available on GitHub. Authors note deviation scores may better capture brain–behavior relationships in smaller clinical samples than raw volumes.

caa10_key_limitations.answer: Normative dataset is cross-sectional; early development (<5 years) not modeled; multi-project, multi-parameter data required ComBat harmonization, limiting direct model portability; potential confounds (medication, lifestyle) may contribute to deviations in SZ.
